obligations.instrument: Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 and DPDP Rules, 2025
obligations.status_note: Rules notified November 2025; substantive notice and consent duties commence May 2027 (18-month phase-in). SPDI Rules, 2011 under the IT Act apply until then.
obligations.requirement: Give candidates a clear, itemised notice of what personal data is processed, for what purpose, and how to exercise their rights, before or at the time consent is sought.
obligations.evidence_needed: Draft candidate privacy notice reviewed by DPO.

obligations.status_note: As above. Whether the employment legitimate-use ground in s. 7 covers applicants (who are not yet employees) needs counsel's view; consent is the safer basis.
obligations.requirement: Identify a lawful ground (consent or a specified legitimate use) for processing candidate data.

obligations.provision: s. 6(1) (consent specific and limited to necessary data)
obligations.requirement: Candidate data is used only for this recruitment purpose; the vendor may not reuse it to train or improve its own products without separate, specific consent.
Where personal data is likely to be used to make a decision that affects the person, ensure it is complete, accurate and consistent. CV parsing errors become decision errors.
obligations.evidence_needed: Parsing accuracy test on a sample of real CVs (including regional formats and non-English names); candidate can view and correct parsed data.

obligations.requirement: A data processor (the vendor) may process candidate data only under a valid contract.

obligations.instrument: Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 and DPDP Rules, 2025
obligations.status_note: As above. Penalty for failure to take reasonable security safeguards can reach Rs 250 crore.
obligations.requirement: Reasonable security safeguards, including at the vendor, to prevent a personal data breach.

obligations.status_note: The Act requires erasure once the purpose is served; the 180-day figure is this organisation's policy.
obligations.requirement: Erase unsuccessful applicants' data within 180 days unless they consent to a talent pool.
obligations.evidence_needed: Retention schedule configured at vendor and verified.

obligations.requirement: An effective grievance mechanism, and a way for candidates to access, correct and erase their data.
obligations.evidence_needed: Named grievance officer and published contact in the candidate notice.

obligations.status_note: The four Labour Codes took effect on 21 November 2025.
obligations.requirement: No discrimination on the ground of gender, including transgender identity, in recruitment for the same or similar work.
obligations.evidence_needed: Gender adverse-impact test shows no statistically significant adverse impact on shadow data.

obligations.requirement: No unfair treatment of transgender persons in recruitment. Testing this requires inclusive, voluntary self-declaration in the audit dataset.
obligations.evidence_needed: Audit self-declaration form with inclusive gender options, held separately from the model.

obligations.instrument: Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016
obligations.status_note: s. 20 binds government establishments; s. 21 requires every establishment to have an equal opportunity policy.
obligations.requirement: Accessible assessment journey and a way to request reasonable accommodation, including assessment without the AI.
obligations.evidence_needed: Accessibility test report; accommodation route in the candidate notice.

obligations.status_note: Non-binding; government policy favours applying existing laws over new AI-specific regulation.
obligations.requirement: A clearly accountable person or function for the AI system's outcomes across its lifecycle.
obligations.evidence_needed: Named accountable executive in the approval record.

obligations.provision: Sutras: Understandable by Design; People First
obligations.requirement: Candidates are told AI is used, and decisions can be explained in terms a person can understand.
obligations.evidence_needed: AI-use notice text; sample individual explanation.

obligations.requirement: Assess the impact of the AI system on individuals and groups before deployment.
obligations.evidence_needed: Completed impact assessment including bias audit.

obligations.requirement: Risks are tracked after deployment, with a response plan for incidents.
obligations.evidence_needed: Monitoring plan with metrics, owners and cadence; incident runbook.

obligations.requirement: Vendor must notify, and the organisation re-test, before any material model change goes live.
The AI can be switched off within one working day, with hiring continuing manually.

disclaimer: Identifies obligations and evidence gaps for the committee. Not legal advice; Legal Counsel confirms applicability before go-live.
